first.rationale: Shorter onboarding directly addresses the completion decline and may also recover activation, with prior evidence of faster time-to-value and broader early adoption. Verify that result against promotional pricing, which addresses the competitive threat more directly but may carry discounting, retention, or customer-quality risks not resolved by the consolidated memory. Current intent is a controlled onboarding experiment, pending archive review.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source directly addresses the current 4% completion decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is rejected despite acquisition lift because verified retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive first renewal. Some uncertainty remains about whether the earlier onboarding effect will replicate under current conditions.

final2.rationale: The doubled volume of price-driven churn conversations materially changes the immediate risk, so run only a tightly bounded pricing experiment for existing, demonstrably price-sensitive SMB accounts. Do not repeat or broadly roll out the verified 40% acquisition discount: it lifted qualified revenue initially but reduced 30-day retention by 12% and failed at renewal. Treat retention-save pricing as a distinct, unproven use case with strict renewal, retained-revenue, and customer-quality guardrails; revert to simplify_onboarding if it does not improve sustainable retained revenue.
